pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.1 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Conversational Skills

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Conversational Skills. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How should we listen for specific information from a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to information from oral texts for communication
2. use appropriate vocabulary to construct sentences

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Conversational Skills helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to readings of texts or recorded audio clips in a group and respond to questions,
2. Work collaboratively to make a list of new vocabulary from the listened-to texts,
3. Construct simple sentences using the new vocabulary from the texts,
4. Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner listens to readings of texts or recorded audio clips actively and responds to questions.
5. Digital literacy: This is enhanced as the learner accesses content when listening to recorded audio clips and responding to questions. Values:

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
